question.text: There is an air bubble of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> in a liquid of surface tension <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>075</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> at a depth of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> below the free surface. The amount by which the pressure inside the bubble is greater than the atmospheric pressure is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math>.

solution.text:
The pressure inside the bubble is given by 

ΔP=P-P0=ρgh+2Tr

The data given is 

r=10-3 mT=0.075 N m-1ρ=1000 kg m-3h=10 cm

Therefore, the pressure in the bubble is 

ΔP=1000×10×10×10-2+2×0.07510-3=1000+150=1150 Pa
